So when we jointly went through this definition of liquid excess reserves, which says like, no, no, not all excess reserves are liquid. We defined this and we designed a control around it, which is in a disclosure in the financial statements that's audited by the, by the board of auditor and gives the board assurance what this is. So we also designed the monitoring process around this. one step further than what we had in 2022. This is a further step where we say in a self financing model where nobody gives you core funding to establish your infrastructure to sustain the organization, an organization has to earn the monies that basically sustain its infrastructure, its business development and similar things, which in other organizations is called the working capital. So here we establish a working capital, but as the same process as we did with liquid excess reserve, we say, well, we have to put safeguards and controls for member states around it by creating disclosures and attach it again to the financial statements so it can be monitored. So we're going actually for it through a development process. But I mean, the definition of excess reserves should be, whatever is left over and not needed to the organization. Liquid excess reserve is not a dividend promise that gets the maximum amount of money out of the organization and at the same time impairing its long-term sustainability.
